subject: Temporal qualification & evidence request for p95 commitments
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@terrahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@terrahealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API p50/p95 commitments — regional measurement ask

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. TerraHealth is evaluating Redwood as our primary hosted inference provider for our clinical triage service.

A couple of questions that came up from legal/procurement:
- Can Redwood commit to p50/p95 latency targets for EU-hosted traffic? Our initial ask is p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 320ms measured at egress in eu-west-1.
- We understand transient regional maintenance and peering incidents happen. Would Redwood accept a temporary qualification window (e.g., 7-day carveout) for scheduled infra upgrades or cloud provider maintenance, and what evidence would you need to grant that?

Procurement would like an evidence package (request matrix + recent per-region latency CSV) and any SLO exceptions language for inclusion in the MSLA.

Can you share a template or an initial response by EOD Tuesday? We're on a tight procurement cadence.

Thanks,

Lina Park
Head of IT Security
TerraHealth

Attachment: terra_slo_request.pdf (pdf)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@terrahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API p50/p95 commitments — regional measurement ask

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear asks and the file.

Short answers:
- We can offer regionally-scoped p50/p95 commitments for Hosted API. For EU (eu-west-1) the standard published targets are p50 <= 100ms, p95 <= 300ms for small-to-medium prompt sizes; for clinical workloads we'll need to scope by payload distribution.
- Temporary qualification windows for scheduled maintenance are possible; we typically allow a defined 'maintenance carveout' with a pre-notice window (48–72h) and require evidence: scheduled maintenance log, impacted node list, and post-event latency report.

I'll coordinate an evidence package and a conditional carveout text. Looping in Kimberly to confirm legal/contract language and Aditya for telemetry export.

Best,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

- Aditya: export the last 30 days of eu-west-1 latency tail and a per-prompt-size histogram (csv). Also include our post-deploy maintenance log template.

Hi Lina (and Procurement team),

Thanks for the patience — attached is the initial evidence package and a narrow carveout template for TerraHealth's review. Summary below:

What Redwood can commit to today (EU / eu-west-1 / hosted):
- Target (proposed contractual language): p50 <= 110ms, p95 <= 310ms measured at egress in eu-west-1 for requests with payloads in the profile provided. We set the p95 using a rolling 30-day measurement window with daily sampling.

Maintenance carveout (proposed narrow scope):
- Allowed for scheduled, pre-notified maintenance with at least 48 hours' notice.
- Max carveout duration per event: 72 hours. One exceptional 7-day carveout may be approved for major infra migrations (requires executive sign-off).
- Required evidence to grant carveout: scheduled maintenance plan, impacted node list, pre/post latency report (we will provide a standard CSV export).

Attachments included:
- redwood_eu_latency_q3.csv (30-day rolling per-region latency summary)
- maintenance_carveout_template.docx (MSLA clause template and required evidence checklist)

Next steps:
- If Procurement is happy with the wording, we can produce a redlined MSLA with the clause and the evidence bundle appended.
- If TerraHealth needs tighter quantiles or a different measurement window, let us know the precise payload profile and volume targets and Aditya will run calibrated numbers.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the evidence package.

Best,
Jonas

--
